extracted.intended_audience: writers of periodical essays and educated general readers (readers/contributors to The Spectator and similar papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for composing short, standalone periodical essays/columns: be concise, lively, and concentrated so each sheet reads like a complete treatise; plus guidance for compiling natural-history species accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate, lively engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: We must immediately fall into our Subject, and treat every Part of it in a lively Manner, or our Papers are thrown by as dull and insipid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid heavy preambles and long wind-ups that are tolerated in bulky volumes; separate papers must engage the reader at once. Each page must get to the point and keep a lively tone throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and concentrated expression (the 'chymical method')
rubrics_metrics.description: An Essay-Writer must practise in the Chymical Method, and give the Virtue of a full Draught in a few Drops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make each sheet a kind of treatise that 'makes out in Thought what it wants in Bulk' — compress meaning and value into small space; avoid relying on length to carry weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make up for lack of bulk by completeness of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Sheet should be a kind of Treatise, and make out in Thought what it wants in Bulk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short paper should touch a subject in its most essential articles so the reader feels the piece is complete despite its small size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of matter or turn of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Matter must lie close together, and either be wholly new in itself, or in the Turn it receives from our Expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either present genuinely new content or present familiar material in a fresh way; mere rehash or flat expressions will be discarded by periodical readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repetitions, tautologies, and enlargements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Subject should be touched upon in its most essential Articles, without the Repetitions, Tautologies and Enlargements, that are indulged to longer Labours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim redundant language and avoid expanding trivial points; brevity must not be filled with needless repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work up a point of humour thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: That a Point of Humour should be worked up in all its Parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the essay contains humorous material, develop it fully within the short piece so the comedic effect is complete and satisfying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to instruct and improve the public (target audience and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common Prints would be of great Use were they thus calculated to diffuse good Sense through the Bulk of a People, to clear up their Understandings, animate their Minds with Virtue, dissipate the Sorrows of a heavy Heart, or unbend the Mind from its more severe Employments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose periodical pieces with the aim of educating and improving the general readership; recognize some readers ('Moles') are incapable or hostile, but target the broader public benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural history species-account requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Royal Society compiled a Body of Natural History, each writer should take a particular species and give a distinct account of its Original, Birth and Education; its Policies, Hostilities and Alliances; the Frame and Texture of its inward and outward Parts; and particularly those that distinguish it from all other Animals, with their peculiar Aptitudes for the State of Being in which Providence has placed them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile accounts from books and observations; be systematic (origin, development, behaviour, anatomy, distinguishing characters, ecological aptitudes). Acknowledge inevitable incompleteness (many species hidden or minute), but use observed species to infer broader conclusions.
